neighbours.label: a settling or dismissive remark that says a matter is acceptable or not worth worrying about (no problem, no big deal, not bad)
fire: The train was a few minutes late. No problem, we still made it.
If the file is missing, just send another copy. No big deal.
The soup was a little cold, but honestly not bad for the price.
You forgot the milk? No worries, I can pick some up later.
The seats are narrow. Still, it is fine for such a short flight.
He missed the first page, but it was no big loss to anyone.
Sorry about the mess! No problem at all, these things happen.
The colour is not what I ordered, but it will do, no harm done.
quiet: The train was a few minutes late, and we missed the connection.
If the file is missing, the auditors will reject the whole claim.
The soup was very cold, and they charged far too much for it.
You forgot the milk again, and now the children have no breakfast.
The seats are narrow, and the flight takes more than eleven hours.
He missed the first page, and that error cost the firm its licence.
They cleaned the mess in the kitchen before the guests arrived.
The colour is not what I ordered, so I am sending it back today.

notes: Top examples are scattered across languages (吧, ' big' deal, 'Sure', ' to' no avail). Sentence-final periods fire at 0.1-0.28 in probes, so a near miss could misfire. Whether 'to no avail' belongs in the same pattern is unsure.
